newsitem.title: PERU: Cook gave lessons to fellow captives in Peru siege.
newsitem.headline: Cook gave lessons to fellow captives in Peru siege.

text.p: Hostages and their guerrilla captors used their time during the three-week-old siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima to receive lessons in Peruvian and Japanese cuisine, a former captive and chef said on Tuesday.

"I mostly taught how to cook ingredients which originated in the Andean region, like corn, potato, pumpkin and tomato. I also gave them tips about Japanese cuisine, like how to select fresh fish," Toshiro Konishi, owner of a Japanese restaurant in Lima, told Reuters.

Confined to a sweaty, cramped room, 38 fellow hostages sat on the floor in a circle for the lessons. They were good pupils, listening attentively and asking questions when they had doubts, Konishi said.
Political debates, chess matches and singing have been among other activities the hostages and their captors have used to keep boredom at bay.
Konishi was among more than 400 hostages already released out of 500 guests captured Dec. 17 when Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas stormed a reception at the residence.
